Where to start

Our Cat Exercise Wheel is designed to give indoor cats a safe, spacious way to run and burn energy. It has a 48-inch outer diameter, a 43-inch inner diameter, a stable base, and smooth inline wheels for a quieter ride. We also offer different traction pad styles, plus an optional light-up LED wheel version.

Good beginner options

LED version of the Cat Exercise Wheel — same wheel, with light-up inline wheels for extra visual fun.

Helpful tip for first-time use

turns.replyText:
Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
Absolutely — here’s the simple version of the main Cat Exercise Wheel options:

1. The wheel itself

Our Cat Exercise Wheel is the main product. It’s the same core wheel, but you choose a few options when ordering.

2. Base color

You can pick:
- Black base
- White base
This is mostly a style choice.

3. Running surface: felt vs. foam

This is the part your cat runs on.



Felt pads: more durable and better if your cat may scratch or stretch on the wheel sometimes.


Foam pads: more soft/cushioned under paw. These come in printed styles like Koi Pond or Tropical Frogs.



Simple way to think about it:
- Want tougher? Choose felt.
- Want softer/funner look? Choose foam.

4. Standard wheels vs. light-up LED wheels

You can choose:
- Standard inline wheels
- Light-up LED inline wheels
The LED option lights up while the wheel spins. No batteries are needed.
Simple way to think about it:
- Want the basic version? Choose standard.
- Want a more playful look? Choose LED.

5. Accessories

A few common add-ons are:



Cat Wheel Chaser Toy - Wheel Bait
Great for beginners. It helps encourage cats to interact with the wheel.


Inline Wheel Kit - Light-up LED
Good if you want to upgrade to LED wheels later.


Base Replacement Kit
This is mainly for replacing parts, not something most first-time buyers need.

- Felt pads if you want durability
- Foam pads if you want a softer feel
- Add Wheel Bait if you want help training your cat to use it

How do I use it properly the very first time?
For the very first use, we recommend:



Take the wheel off the base and lay it on its side on the floor for the first few days.


Use treats or toys to gently encourage your cat to approach and sniff it.


Never force your cat onto or near the wheel.


Keep it on the floor until your cat seems relaxed around it.


Then put it back on the base and continue slowly.



The key is to go slow and be patient.
